warmup: grep -lE 'trap .* EXIT' test/*.sh | xargs grep -LE 'trap .*(INT|TERM|HUP)' | wc -l
description:
THE BEHAVIOURAL SUITE READS THE HOST IT RUNS ON, AND THAT MADE ONE VERIFY TAKE SIX HOURS.

MEASURED 2026-09-18 on an operator host with three other chief runs live (14 physical cores). In one verify, tests 1–33 of the 78-test behavioural block took twelve minutes; `test/suspectlimit.sh` then took six hours. Its fixture run logged `⏸ machine budget hold — machine load: load average 17.04 over 14 core(s)`: the fixture's `chief run -p 4` launched two of its four tasklists and held the other two until the HOST's load average fell below the ceiling. The host did not sleep (`pmset -g log` shows no sleep or wake in the window). Reproduced on `main` in a scratch worktree the next day with the same hold. 53 of the 96 test scripts start a real `chief run`; only `test/load-admission.sh` and `test/concurrency-monitor.sh` pin the load inputs they depend on.

THE SAME FIXTURE READ THE HOST'S WORKTREES. Its startup sweep listed the operator's real `~/.chief/worktrees/*` entries (`LEFT ALONE, a live run is behind it`). It left them alone, but a hermetic test has no business enumerating them — that is the class of the 2026-08-17 incident, where a sweep destroyed a run in another repository.

AND IT LEAVES ITS TEMP DIRECTORIES WHEN STOPPED. 92 of 96 test scripts clean up with `trap … EXIT` only. A non-interactive bash killed by SIGTERM or SIGHUP does not run the EXIT trap, so every interrupted verify strands its `mktemp` trees: 385 `tmp.*` directories were found in one operator's `$TMPDIR`.

userStories.title: A fixture run does not wait on the host's load
userStories.description: Tests that start a real run are isolated from the host's machine budget unless the budget is what they test.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared test helper (or the install step every such test uses) exports `CHIEF_MACHINE_LOAD_LIMIT=off` for fixture runs; the tests that exercise the load or turn budget (`test/load-admission.sh`, `test/concurrency-monitor.sh`, `test/machine-budget.sh`, `test/gate-budget.sh`, `test/concurrency.sh`) keep pinning their own values and still pass.

Proven by running `test/suspectlimit.sh` with a synthetic high load reading (e.g. `CHIEF_LOAD_AVERAGE=62` exported by the caller): it completes in its normal time, not held. Record both timings in the notes.
A guard (in `test/bystander.sh` or a new test) fails when a fixture run's log contains `machine budget hold` while the test did not ask for a budget.
userStories.notes: test/lib.sh sourced by all 96 test scripts (folded onto the `ROOT=` line — see below); CHIEF_MACHINE_LOAD_LIMIT resolves to `off` unless requested. The five capacity tests keep their own pins and are green: load-admission PASS, concurrency-monitor PASS, machine-budget PASS, gate-budget PASS, concurrency PASS. TIMINGS for test/suspectlimit.sh on a 14-core host: baseline 11.304s total (exit 0), with CHIEF_LOAD_AVERAGE=62 exported by the caller 10.594s total (exit 0) — identical within noise, no hold logged, and its own `chief ps` render reads `load average: 62 / 14 physical core(s) · ceiling off`. GUARD: new test/host-isolation.sh, PASS in 15.753s — PART A runs -p 2 under a staged live gate and a reported load of 62 and asserts no `machine budget hold` in the log plus both tasklists merged; PART B is the mutation control (CHIEF_MACHINE_LOAD_LIMIT=4, the pre-lib.sh reading) and the same fixture DOES hold, by name (`machine budget hold — machine load: load average 62 over 4 core(s)`), proving PART A discriminates; PART C pins that an explicit request survives lib.sh. Registered in all three gate lists (.chief/verify.sh CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS, test/all.sh BASH_SUITE, .github/workflows/ci.yml; ci.yml re-validated with yaml.safe_load). The first attempt inserted the source as its OWN line and `chief verify` BLOCKED on the quality ratchet: duplicate_blocks 224 -> 235 (delta +11, tolerance 0), because the dup window is 6 normalized lines and the suite preamble was already 5; folding the source onto the ROOT line restores duplicate_blocks 224 -> 224 (delta 0) with every other tracked metric at delta 0. Re-run after the fold: host-isolation, load-admission, concurrency-monitor, machine-budget, gate-budget, concurrency, smoke, noworkguard, doc-claims, version-bump all PASS; bash -n clean across test/*.sh.

userStories.title: A fixture run never sees the host's worktrees
userStories.description: Every test that starts a driver gives it a private worktree root.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixture runs set `CHIEF_WORKTREE_ROOT` to a directory inside the test's own temp tree; no test's run log names a path under the real `~/.chief/worktrees`.
A guard fails a test whose fixture run logs a `>> startup:` line for a path outside the test's temp tree.
userStories.notes: test/lib.sh pins CHIEF_PREFIX (not CHIEF_WORKTREE_ROOT) to a private per-pid root under $TMPDIR, so chief_worktree_root() resolves inside the test process rather than to ~/.chief/worktrees. The root is the LAST word on worktree placement and pinning it at source time would overrule the dozen tests that pin the tree themselves (pause/plan-review/overlap-zones read $CHIEF_PREFIX/worktrees/*/<name>; reapscope/reapenv/reap-escaped/bystander BUILD the tree the sweep under test walks) — the prefix fills only the silence, and a later assignment still wins. MEASURED on the incident host: ~/.chief/worktrees held 136 entries, 129 of them EMPTY husks (one per fixture repo path: cli-* from provider-conformance, proj-* from status-deps, repo-* from ~60 more). After the fix, 49 test scripts run back to back left the count at 136 -> 136, and 0 leftover temp roots. PINNED UNCONDITIONALLY, unlike the load ceiling: `chief verify` exports CHIEF_PREFIX=/Users/<op>/.chief into every hook, so ${CHIEF_PREFIX:-} would be a no-op exactly when it matters; the override gets its own name, CHIEF_TEST_PREFIX. Nothing is created (paths.sh resolves, never mkdirs), and the one husk a driver-running test leaves is reclaimed by the next test to source lib.sh (pid-keyed name, owned by us, not a symlink, pid dead) rather than by a trap, since all 96 scripts replace the EXIT trap two lines below. GUARD: test/host-isolation.sh PARTS D and E, PASS in 41.130s (whole file, all five parts). PART D plants a worktree-shaped dir at the <root>/<repo>/<wt> depth the sweep accepts, runs -p 2, and asserts >=1 `>> startup:` verdict (1 observed) with every one inside the test's own temp trees; PART E is the mutation control — `env -u CHIEF_PREFIX -u CHIEF_TEST_PREFIX HOME=<decoy temp tree>` restores the pre-fix chain and the SAME fixture walks $HOME/.chief/worktrees, which PART D's check names, so PART D is not vacuous. The decoy $HOME is a temp tree of the test's own: a control for "a fixture reads the real ~/.chief" may not itself read the real ~/.chief. REGRESSION: 49 scripts PASS, including every prefix-sensitive one — container, reapscope, reapenv, reap-escaped, monitor-orphan, sweep, bystander-adjacent monitor-orphan, pause, plan-review, overlap-zones, status-scope/json/categories/deps/perf-adjacent, park-reasons, update-reroot, version-bump, doc-sync, doc-claims, events, headless, account-env, smoke, noworkguard, crossrepo, usage, quality-ratchet, provider-conformance, and the five capacity tests (load-admission, concurrency-monitor, machine-budget, gate-budget, concurrency). bash -n clean across test/*.sh, engine/*.sh and bin/chief; quality ratchet delta 0 on every tracked metric.

userStories.title: An interrupted suite leaves nothing behind
userStories.description: Temp directories are removed when a test is interrupted, not only when it exits normally.
acceptanceCriteria: Every test script that creates a temp tree traps INT, TERM and HUP as well as EXIT (by a shared helper rather than 96 copies), so the cleanup runs when the script is signalled.
Proven by starting `test/all.sh` (or the bystander block), sending SIGTERM mid-run, and listing `$TMPDIR` before and after: no new `tmp.*` tree survives. Record the counts.
The decoy and bystander lifetimes in `test/bystander.sh` are unchanged (they are bounded by their parent since `127`).
userStories.notes: test/lib.sh traps INT · TERM · HUP once at source time; each handler restores the default disposition, deletes lib.sh's own prefix root and calls `exit 128+n`, which runs each script's EXISTING EXIT trap unchanged — one rule instead of three signals × 96 files, and no second copy of any cleanup. CRITERION 2, MEASURED: `bash test/all.sh` in its own process group, group SIGTERM 120s in (11 tests complete, test/admission-refusals.sh interrupted), $TMPDIR counted before and after — tmp.* 67 -> 68 at the signal -> 67 after; chief-test-host.* 0 -> 0 -> 0; all.sh exited 143; `find -mmin -6` names no survivor from the run. THE PREMISE WAS FALSE AND MEASURING IT MOVED THE TARGET: on bash 3.2.57 (the system bash here) an untrapped INT/TERM/HUP runs the EXIT trap on its way out — pid- and group-addressed, in a builtin or blocked in a foreground child alike — so `$WORK` was never what an interrupted run stranded. Two things were: (a) lib.sh's PREFIX ROOT, which no test's EXIT trap has heard of, and (b) the STATUS — a pid-addressed SIGINT with nothing trapped exits the shell ZERO, so all.sh/bystander.sh/verify.sh read a killed test as a PASS; with the handler it is 130/143/129 every time. THE FIRST interrupted run left exactly ONE tree, and it was not a signal problem: test/admission-refusals.sh's `[ -n "$HOLDER_PID" ] && kill …` returns non-zero under `set -euo pipefail`, which ENDS THE SHELL inside the trap before `rm -rf "$WORK"` — repaired there and in test/unavailnote.sh, and test/signal-cleanup.sh PART D now scans the suite for the shape (0 findings; it still flags the removed line, so it is not vacuous). Also repaired test/host-isolation.sh PART B, which killed the run SHIM while the driver went on writing into $WORK as `rm -rf` walked it (3 leaked trees on this host): launched with `set -m`, stopped by GROUP, and it now leaks none — PASS in 24.5s, $TMPDIR dirs 4 -> 4. GUARD: new test/signal-cleanup.sh, PASS in 7.3s — PART A three signals × the four EXIT-trap shapes in this suite, each victim under a private $TMPDIR (residue counted exactly) and signalled by group: empty every time, status 130/143/129; PART B the mutation control (the three trap lines sed'd out of a copy of lib.sh) leaves the prefix root behind for all three signals; PART C pins the deferral bound as a FLOOR (3s); PART D the errexit-cleanup scan. Registered in all three gate lists (.chief/verify.sh CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS, test/all.sh BASH_SUITE, .github/workflows/ci.yml — re-validated with yaml.safe_load). CRITERION 3: test/bystander.sh is untouched, and `CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS="signal-cleanup host-isolation smoke teardown" bash test/bystander.sh` -> BYSTANDER PASS, both decoys alive after every test, "no fixture leaked". CONTEXT for the 385: of the 69 $TMPDIR entries on this host 62 are FILES, 9 KB copies of the agent prompt written once per turn by the live driver's provider invocation — a clean `bash test/smoke.sh` leaks none (69 -> 69), so the suite is not their author. `bash -n` clean across test/*.sh; quality ratchet delta 0 on every tracked metric.

userStories.title: Find out whether a fixture writes into the host's run records
userStories.description: Explain one unexplained observation, and fix it if it is real.
acceptanceCriteria: OBSERVED 2026-09-18: while a real run's verify was executing the suite, that real run's `<state>/parallel/<name>.live.json` read `phase: provider-unavailable`, `total: 1`, `noturn: 3/3` — the shape of a fixture scenario — while `chief ps` showed the real run at 3/3 in an agent turn.

Determine whether any test writes to the host's state directory (for example through an inherited environment variable naming it), and either fix the leak with a guard test, or record in the notes the measured explanation and why it is harmless.
userStories.notes: YES — real, reproduced on demand, and worse than the observation. MECHANISM: `chief verify` runs the suite from inside an agent turn and driver.sh's run_worker exports the run's own state into it — 36 CHIEF_* variables, of which agent.sh reads five as absolute paths INTO A LIVE RUN: CHIEF_LIVE_FILE (live_set), CHIEF_EVENTS_FILE (event_emit), CHIEF_PRD_SNAPSHOT (_prd_promote, and agent.sh SEEDS FROM it), CHIEF_VERIFY_CACHE_STATE (verify_cache_record) and CHIEF_ITER_HOOK, which is EVAL'D — a real `driver.sh --integrate-base <the real branch> <the real worktree> <the real repo> main`. 26 test scripts drive engine/agent.sh directly; 6 pin CHIEF_LIVE_FILE and 2 `env -u` a handful, so the hazard was known in two files as a local workaround, and the other 18 inherit everything. MEASURED 2026-09-19 with each pointer aimed at a canary and three UNMODIFIED tests run (ratelimit, provider-unavailable, provider): all three reported PASS and between them they (a) rewrote the live record to `phase=stalled story=US-1 total=1 stall=2/2 noturn=3/3` — this criterion's observation verbatim, a one-story fixture's shape over a four-story run; (b) appended 55 event lines carrying the REAL runId, repo and tasklist name, including `HTTP 401 (authentication_error) — permanent refusal (the credential is wrong, revoked…)`; (c) replaced snapshots/128-….json with {"branchName":"chief/provider",…}; (d) RAN the iteration hook. Backwards too: two tests sharing the inherited snapshot contaminated each other, and test/provider.sh FAILED (`devin agent failed`) under the polluted env and PASSES under the fix — the leak was already costing a red test. DAMAGE REPAIRED in place (snapshot re-banked from this worktree's prd.json; live record rewritten with live_set). FIX in test/lib.sh: every CHIEF_* in the environment is unset at source time and what stays is NAMED — CHIEF_TEST_*, CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS (scrub it and the merge gate's behavioural block runs EMPTY reporting PASS), CHIEF_VERIFY_TESTS, and the CHIEF_MACHINE_*/CHIEF_LOAD_AVERAGE capacity NUMBERS, less the hand-named CHIEF_MACHINE_BUDGET_LOG, which is a path wearing the capacity prefix and was measured surviving v1 of the rule. A denylist would rot: 11 of the 28 names the driver hands an agent turn were added in the last five weeks. GUARD: test/host-isolation.sh PARTS F/G/H, whole file PASS in 50.4s (8 parts). F derives the roster FROM driver.sh (two parsers, one per shape; 28 names found, floor of 20, five asserted individually so a moved anchor FAILS) and asserts none survives lib.sh, plus that CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS comes through untouched. G drives engine/agent.sh with every pointer aimed at a canary laid out as a live run's state root — two fixtures, because a refusing agent never reaches an iteration boundary and a COMPLETE turn leaves the loop above one, so the completing fixture takes TWO turns — and all seven writes are checked. H is the mutation control, a NEUTERED COPY of lib.sh (no configuration restores a rule), and it reproduces all four incident writes: live record rewritten, PRD snapshot overwritten, 9 event lines appended, iteration hook EXECUTED; it is asserted BY NAME on the first two. REGRESSION: 15 of the 26 exposed scripts run standalone under this branch — ratelimit, provider-unavailable, provider, provider-backoff, provider-credit, provider-conformance, stall-flag, stream-activity, verify-cache, verify-stream, liveliness, limitstate, limitresume, limitmonitor, suspectlimit — all PASS, 0 FAIL; the rest are covered by the 76-test bystander block in the gate below. `bash -n` clean across test/*.sh; quality ratchet delta 0 on every tracked metric; scripts/check-doc-links.mjs 0 dead references.
